Политика выгружается как `policy.onnx` (: The policy is exported as `policy.onnx` (obs [1, 490] → actions [1, 29], normalization inside) with a `deploy.yaml` for `g1_ctrl` from unitree_rl_mjlab, and run in unitree_mujoco under Ubuntu (WSL2) with a virtual gamepad. A recorder rebuilds g1_ctrl's observation from `lowstate` and matches the ONNX output to `lowcmd` within ~1e-7 rad. 155 bridge runs so far. Along the way four gaps turned up — each with a patch and a measurement:
Такт FSM может скопировать вектор действ: The FSM tick can copy the action vector before the first policy step: one `lowcmd` with q = 0 on all 29 joints at Velocity gains (2 of 11 entries). Patch: hold the previous target until the first step. Since then: no zero-target message in any entry.
Масштабирование и ограничение идут двумя: Scaling and clamping run in two loops while the 1 kHz tick copies without a lock — an ankle roll 0.63 rad past its limit (~18 N·m for ~1 ms). Stress test: 91% of copies out of clip → 0 with a mutex; bridge 0 of 202,500 messages.
Проверка падения — заглушка: The fall check is a stub
`acos(−g_z) > limit` закомментировано, и: `acos(−g_z) > limit` is commented out and it returns false, so a fallen robot stays in Velocity. Patch: the same test on the IMU of each tick. 3 of 3 falls → Passive at 57.5–57.9°, 0 false triggers in 7 scenarios.
Робота нечем толкнуть: Nothing to push the robot with
Клавиши цифрового блока прикладывают к т: Numpad keys apply a pelvis force M·Δv/0.1 s (Δv 0.5–2.25 m/s, M = 35.112 kg) in the heading frame, logged per push — the push the training now reproduces to 1e-8 in qvel.
Поставляемая политика скорости (v0) в то: The shipped velocity policy (v0) run in the same CPU harness: our physics with Unitree's motor curves, same seeds. v0 was not run in the real bridge. Where v0 is better, it says so.

We check the policy not only in our own simulator. The network is saved in the format Unitree's own robot-control program (`g1_ctrl`) reads and runs in their simulator (`unitree_mujoco`) — the same program that will run on the real robot — driven by a virtual gamepad, the way a person drives it with the remote. A separate check compares the numbers: what Unitree's program feeds the network and what goes to the motors match our computation to 0.0000001 rad. 199 runs in this setup so far. On the way we found five places where something did not work as it should; each has a fix and a measurement.
Рывок при включении ходьбы: A jerk when walking mode starts
При переключении в режим ходьбы программ: When switching into walking mode the program could, for one millisecond, send all 29 motors to the zero angle — already at walking stiffness, a jerk in every joint. It happened in 2 of 11 switches. The fix holds the previous pose until the network's first answer; not one such jerk since.
Программа сначала масштабирует ответ сет: The program scales the network's answer and then clips it to the joint limits in two passes, while another thread copies those numbers 1,000 times a second without waiting. Sometimes an unclipped value reached the motors — e.g. an ankle 0.63 rad past its limit, about 18 N·m for roughly 1 ms. In a stress test 91% of copies were corrupt; with a lock that forbids copying mid-way, none. In Unitree's simulator: 0 bad commands out of 202,500.
Проверка падения выключена: The fall check is switched off
В коде есть проверка «наклонился сильнее: The code has a check 'tilted past the limit — release the motors', but its working line is commented out and the function always answers 'not fallen': a fallen robot keeps trying to walk. The fix runs the same check on the tilt sensor every tick: 3 of 3 falls → motors released at 57.5–57.9° of tilt, 0 false triggers in 7 scenarios.
В симуляторе Unitree нельзя ударить робо: Unitree's simulator cannot hit the robot with a known force. We added keys that push the pelvis with an exact impulse (mass × change of speed over 0.1 s, Δv 0.5–2.25 m/s) and log every push. Training now reproduces exactly this push.
Стопы проходили друг сквозь друга: The feet passed through each other
В симуляторе Unitree (и у нас раньше) ст: In Unitree's simulator (and in ours before) a foot touches the world only with points on its sole, while the model Unitree itself trains on gives each foot 7 capsules with friction. Without them one foot could pass through the other and neither simulator saw it — on a robot that is a trip. With Unitree's capsules in training, side steps of ±1 m/s cross the feet in 0–0.3% of steps instead of 9–10%, and sideways pushes no longer knock the robot down.
Политику ходьбы, которую Unitree поставл: We ran the walking policy Unitree ships with the robot (v0) in the same harness as ours: our physics with Unitree's motor curves, the same starts. It was not run in Unitree's simulator. Where v0 is better, the table says so.
Уползание через 2–6 с после остановки с: Creep 2–6 s after a stop from 1.5 / 2 m/s

В обучении курс держался сам: стоило роб: In training the heading held on its own: as soon as the robot began to turn during a side step, the turn command corrected it. The policy had got used to this hint, and the penalty saw a drift of 0.02 rad/s instead of the real 0.12. The robot's stick has no such hint. Now the side step is learned without it, as with the stick: candidate 8 at the stick's limit ±0.5 m/s has a drift of −0.002…+0.011 rad/s, while candidate 7 drifted −0.036…−0.040 rad/s on a side step to the right, which is −20…−22° in 10 s.
В обучении курс подправлялся сам, и поли: In training the heading was corrected on its own, and the policy relied on that; the robot's stick does not do this. In the clip, a step to the right at 0.5 m/s without the hint: candidate 7 turns (in the Unitree stack −20…−22° in 10 s), candidate 8, which learned without it, walks straight. At the same time it turned out that the stop after a side step depended on motor friction — now it is randomised in training.
